To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

elastic proton scattering in combination with the Glauber approach provides a very effective tool for determining the size and shape of nuclear-matter distributions of exotic nuclei, that this technique is well suited for probing halo nuclei and that the present data on 6He, 8He and 11Li provide the most accurate information on nuclear-matter densities of these nuclei to date.

the elastic scattering method is a powerful and reliable tool for investigating halo structures, that 6He and especially 8He have a pronounced neutron halo, and that 11Li exhibits the most extended halo of all investigated nuclei.
elastic proton scattering at intermediate energies is a very sensitive method to probe the size and the shape of nuclear-matter density distribution of exotic nuclei.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of nuclear structure of light exotic nuclei by probing the nuclear-matter distributions of these nuclei with the aid of elastic proton scattering.
probing the nuclear-matter density distribution of neutron-rich light nuclei, in particular of those exhibiting a halo structure.
the investigation of exotic nuclei with neutron halos, using the elastic proton scattering method in inverse kinematics with the hydrogen-filled ionisation chamber IKAR.

the present results are in agreement with the concept of halo nuclei and with the predictions from microscopic calculations.

the nuclear-matter distributions of the halo nuclei 6He and, in particular, 8He are in agreement with the predictions from microscopic cluster-model calculations, whereas those of the Li isotopes are not.
the present data are in excellent agreement with the concept of halo nuclei.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present method of proton scattering in inverse-kinematics experiments is an effective means for probing the nuclear-matter distributions of exotic nuclei.

the elastic proton scattering in combination with the Glauber theory is an excellent tool for studying the nuclear matter distributions in halo nuclei, in particular for the determination of the size and the radial shape of the halo.
the elastic proton scattering method in inverse kinematics is a very promising tool for probing nuclear-matters distributions in halo nuclei.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the elastic-proton scattering technique in inverse kinematics is a very powerful tool for studying nuclear-matter density profiles and the structure of exotic nuclei.
elastic proton scattering in the intermediate energy region provides a powerful tool for studying the nuclear-structure properties of exotic nuclei.

the method of elastic scattering is a powerful and versatile tool for investigating nuclear-matter distributions and for probing the structure of exotic nuclei, especially of those with a halo structure.
